requirement:
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.references.outline_selectors`. I did not request implementation source.

- **Path from root, and the empty selector selects the root.**
  - `outline/tests.rs#fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` builds and resolves nested selectors such as `mod[local]/fn[run]` and `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`. It asserts that `resolve("")` returns node 0.
  - `selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments]` checks that `parse_selector("")` is empty. It also checks that malformed paths are rejected, including `a//b`, `fn`, `fn[run`, `[run]` and `fn[run]x`.
- **Named segment `kind[name]`.** The Rust test asserts that every expected selector appears in the outline and round-trips through `resolve`. This covers impl, trait, extern, macro and other kinds. The parse test covers the named label with a multi-part name.
- **Anonymous segment `kind@<first 12 hex digits of the identity hash>`.**
  - `fn[anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes]` checks the `use@` prefix and a length of 12 hex digits.
  - `fn[anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits]` asserts that the selector equals `pair[items]/item@{identity_hash[..12]}`. It also asserts that the identity hash differs from the structural hash. After a descendant edit, the identity hash and selector stay the same and the selector still resolves.
  - The parse test normalizes the hash to lowercase and rejects the short hash `use@123`.
- **`#N` disambiguation, one-based and in source order.**
  - The Rust test checks `fn[repeated]#1` and `#2`, and checks that the ambiguous `fn[repeated]` fails to resolve. It also checks that `fn[missing]` fails.
  - The `use` test asserts that two identical `use` nodes get `#1` then `#2`, in source order.
  - The parse test checks that the ordinal is parsed and that `#0` is rejected.
- **`line` nodes are interchangeable.** `fn[plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes]` shows that two identical lines get identical `line@` selectors with no `#N`. It also shows that the shared selector resolves.
- **Percent-encoding.**
  - `fn[names_round_trip_through_percent_encoding]` asserts the exact encoding of space, `/`, `[`, `]`, `#`, `@`, `%`, tab, no-break space and ideographic space. It checks that non-ASCII `é` is kept as is, while the two multi-byte spaces are encoded as UTF-8 bytes. It checks decode round-trips and rejects raw `/`, a bad `%zz` escape and raw whitespace.
  - The Rust test's `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]` selector shows that real node names are encoded.
  - `fn[profile_rules_map_only_matching_contexts_and_keep_other_nodes_transparent]` checks the malformed-escape error path.
- **No line numbers in selectors.**
  - In the `use` test, selectors generated before inserting lines still resolve after the insertion shifts the line numbers.
  - No test selector contains line positions.

The structural-hash details are covered by their own requirement. This requirement only cites it for the 12-digit identity-hash prefix, and that prefix is tested. I found no obligation without a test and no weak assertion, so I found no gaps.

text: :::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
